column1: # The limitations of one tool's exposure report, one row per limitation. Read
# check decides whether the row is printed for this repository:
#   present   printed when a file in scope matches pattern, a shell case glob
# A row is a statement about what this report cannot know, printed only where it
# is true of the repository being scanned. A report that repeats every caveat
# every time teaches a reader to skip them.

column4: User and organization memory loads in every session and sits outside any repository, so this report cannot see it: the user-level and managed instruction files, a home rules directory, and the per-project auto-memory directory whose index is loaded at every session start.

Settings files are not read. An exclusion list, a setting-sources flag or a project-instructions setting can add or remove files from the surfaces above, so a file called automatic here can be excluded for a given run.
An agent-instruction file is present. Whether it is read at all also depends on the absence of a project instruction file above the repository, which a scan of this repository cannot determine.

An instruction file is present. Claude Code skips one larger than 4 MiB, and loads only the first 200 lines or 25KB of the auto-memory index, so a file on a surface above can still be dropped for size.
Cursor user rules live in settings and in a home rules directory, and team rules live on Cursor's servers. Neither is in a repository, so neither appears above.
A rule whose frontmatter cannot be read is reported as unknown rather than assumed to load or not to load.
A rules directory below the repository root is not modelled: the rules reference places project rules in .cursor/rules at the project root, and says nothing about a second one further down.
A .cursorrules file is present. The current Cursor rules reference does not mention it, so this report cannot say whether it is still read.
The Codex home directory is outside any repository. An override file there is read first and can replace what this report describes.
The fallback-filename setting lives in the user's own config rather than in a repository and is not read here, so a repository relying on it is under-reported.

Codex follows only the root-to-working-directory path, and this report does not know the directory a session starts in. It also stops adding files once the combined size reaches its project document byte cap (32 KiB by default), so a file that is on a surface above can still be past the cap or off the path.

A path-specific instruction file can carry an excludeAgent field withdrawing it from code review or the cloud agent. Only applyTo is read here, so such a file is reported by its path rather than by that field.
Personal and organization instructions are configured outside the repository and are not visible to this report.
Code review reads instructions from the head branch of a pull request rather than the branch this scan ran on.
Path-specific instructions are documented as reaching the cloud agent and code review, so their effect elsewhere is not modeled.

The generic model covers the agent-instruction file only. Every other tool's private surfaces are out of scope by definition, so a file with no surface here is reported as unknown rather than as unexposed.
